output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets had roughly doubled since August and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix whatever was causing wrong bills (CL-01). Investigation showed response times were within SLA (E-01), contradicting that framing, and traced the surge to a billing-import rule: BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling, while firmware v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 units (E-14); this misclassifies valid high-volume reads as 'high consumption' and rejects them, forcing estimate-substituted bills. Of 1240 disputed bills on ESTIMATED reads (E-02), 1184 were confirmed (E-12, cross-checked by E-15/E-16/E-17) to be AMI reads received and exported but rejected via REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION. An earlier framing centered on a field-route completion shortfall (PD-1@v1) was invalidated once E-12 showed the disputed-estimated population was AMI/import-driven, not missing-manual-read-driven. The release delivers a bill_adjustment_candidates list identifying the 1184/1240 affected accounts for manual correction by Billing Operations under K-BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes); decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the remaining open high-impact questions concern scope outside what was actually released.
key_points: Initial request (CL-01, SH-CS) blamed slow ticket response; E-01 shows median 1.6-day / p90 2.8-day response times, within the 3.0-day SLA, contradicting that claim.
Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) per E-03; no tariff change was found (E-04) to explain it.

1240 of disputed bills were tied to ESTIMATED reads vs 1785 ACTUAL (E-02); 1184 of the 1240 were AMI reads received before cutoff and exported but rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on billing import (E-12), independently confirmed by E-15, E-16 and E-17.

Rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling=none (E-13), compares raw register values directly to m3 history; firmware v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), causing valid reads to be spuriously flagged as high consumption.

A prior problem framing (PD-1@v1, field-route completion shortfall, E-05) was invalidated once E-12 showed the disputed-estimated population was AMI-channel/import-rejection driven rather than tied to missing manual field reads; this also invalidated several linked assumptions, hypotheses, remedies and work items (dependency review DR-1).

The release scope delivered is limited to identify_bill_adjustment_candidates:DA-BILL, producing an account-level list of the 1184/1240 confirmed affected accounts for manual review and correction by SH-BILL (Billing Operations), consistent with K-BILLWRITE's no-automated-write requirement.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; the DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred open questions tracked as verification obligations whose blocking_scope (DA-MDMS/DA-TICKET/DA-RULES actions) lies outside the released DA-BILL scope.
limitations_explained: The problem-definition gate for this fix passed conditionally, with some open questions deferred and tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.

VOB-U-RULE-SCOPE-OTHER-METERS remains open: it is unknown how many accounts beyond the 1240 disputed ones (including customers who have not filed a dispute) were affected by the BV-17 misclassification; this is outside the released scope.

VOB-U-SURGE-ATTRIBUTION-COMPLETENE remains open: it is unconfirmed whether fixing BV-17 fully explains the Aug-Sep dispute doubling, or whether the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes and the 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED accounts (E-12) also contribute; this too is outside the released scope.
Correcting BV-17 is known to address only the 1184-of-1240 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern; other dispute populations are a tracked limitation, not resolved by this release.
DA-MDMS data-asset completeness is UNKNOWN, so any future attempt to enumerate the full affected meter population may undercount accounts beyond the 1240 already disputed.
CRM ticket data (DA-TICKET) is free text with UNKNOWN completeness, so classifying disputes by cause risks misclassifying ambiguous tickets, leaving residual uncertainty for non-BV-17 causes.

The actual BV-17 unit-scaling fix is a change to a read-only tool surface (DA-RULES); this release can only specify and hand off that fix for Billing Operations to deploy, not deploy or re-verify it directly.
Two HIGH-impact VOBs remain OPEN, which narrows the released scope to the already-confirmed 1184/1240 account population rather than any broader population.
